signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Disadvantage
signals.text: CHF leads G10 performance with a 1W average gain of +1.167% across 6 pairs, while AUD lags at -0.666% across 4 pairs, creating an extreme 1.832% spread. The pair trades at 0.5536, with AUD/USD remaining pinned in a clear downtrend below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.6803/0.6925/0.7037. The RBA cash rate at 4.85% vs SNB 0.00% delivers a 485bp nominal carry advantage to AUD, yet CHF safe-haven demand completely overrides this yield premium amid VIX holding at 26.8. Furthermore, Swiss macroeconomic momentum outpaces Australia, as reflected in the CHF ESI of +20.1 against the AUD ESI of -10.1. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF, momentum and safe-haven flows dominating carry. Catalyst: RBA meeting 8 Dec — hold priced. Risk: Broad cross-asset volatility retreats with VIX dropping below 20, triggering carry-seeking flows back into high-yielding AUD.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention Risk + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 159.298, trading just below the critical 160.00 intervention threshold and above its SMA20/50/200 moving-average band at 158.90/158.25/158.95. The 1M 25d risk reversal reflects severe downside hedging at -1.85, showing aggressive institutional demand for JPY calls despite Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% offering a +275bp carry buffer. Tokyo Core CPI just printed hot at 2.9% YoY against a 2.8% forecast, intensifying domestic pressure on the Bank of Japan ahead of its policy meeting. At the same time, VIX sits elevated at 26.8, and the correlation between USD/JPY and VIX has flipped negative to -0.162 (z=-2.29σ), confirming safe-haven dynamics are re-engaging. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish USD/JPY, intervention overhang capping upside. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Dec — hike bias active. Risk: MoF remains passive on a test of 160.00, allowing positive carry to extend spot higher.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short + ECB Leadership Shift
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.0973, holding below its daily SMA20 at 1.1074, SMA50 at 1.1189, and SMA200 at 1.1487. CFTC data shows leveraged funds heavily net short EUR by -105,891 contracts, positioned at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range with z=-1.68, reflecting an extremely crowded institutional short. Headlines confirm Pablo Hernández de Cos will succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB President, arriving alongside published minutes highlighting a tightening bias. Although Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% maintains a 135bp carry advantage supporting the dollar, EUR/USD screens as deeply cheap on fair value at z=-2.79σ against a model benchmark of 1.1155. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD mean-reversion, short-squeeze potential against crowded specs. Catalyst: France and Spain flash CPI prints due 07:45–08:00 UTC. Risk: Eurozone inflation prints miss expectations, reinforcing structural dollar carry dominance.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Positioning vs Retail Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5471, locked in a structural downtrend below falling moving averages with SMA20 at 0.5542 and SMA50 at 0.5608. Leveraged funds hold a substantial net short of -23,862 contracts (pctl 23), whereas retail sentiment is 92% long, creating an acute institutional-versus-retail divergence. New Zealand data remains deeply depressed with the NZD Economic Surprise Index printing at -15.4, while falling fuel prices have cooled consumer inflation fears. Furthermore, the Fed at 4.00% vs RBNZ at 2.75% provides a +125bp carry advantage favoring the dollar. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, retail capitulation risk in force. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 9 Dec — hike bias active. Risk: Retail longs clear without triggering a stop run and RBNZ delivers a hawkish surprise.
